title: Replicator fails to process instances (containers or virtual machines) that are deployed on cluster members other than the one where the `replicator run` command is executed.
description:
### Please confirm

- [x] I have searched existing issues to check if an issue already exists for the bug I encountered.

### Distribution

Ubuntu

### Distribution version

24.04 LTS

### Output of `snap list --all lxd core20 core22 core24 snapd`

```shell
root@micro1:~# snap list --all lxd core20 core22 core24 snapd
Name    Version      Rev    Tracking       Publisher   Notes
core24  20260317     1587   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
lxd     git-83beb32  39247  latest/edge    canonical✓  in-cohort
snapd   2.75.2       26865  latest/stable  canonical✓  snapd
```

### System info

kernel_version: 6.8.0-106-generic
driver_version: 6.0.0 | 10.2.1
server_version: "6.8"
storage: cephfs | zfs | ceph


### Instance log

N.A.

### Expected behavior

The replicator transfers all instances in a project (containers or VMs) with snapshots.


### Actual behavior

The replicator fails to process instances (containers or VMs) that are located on a cluster member other than the one where the replicator command is initiated. Specifically, it neither takes snapshots nor transfers these remote instances to the target cluster.

### Steps to reproduce


**Environment**
**Setup**: Two MicroClouds (A and B) deployed on separate physical hosts via [Terraform](https://github.com/canonical/microcloud/tree/main/demos/terraform).
**Resources**: 4GiB RAM per MicroCloud instance (required to avoid DB time-skew errors).
**Connectivity**: Routes manually configured to allow bidirectional communication between the 10.x.x.x subnets via the host IPs.

**Step to reproduce**

1. Deploy 2 MicroClouds A and B in two different hosts A and B. 
```
root@micro1:~# snap list
Name        Version                 Rev    Tracking       Publisher   Notes
core24      20260317                1587   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
lxd         git-83beb32             39247  latest/edge    canonical✓  in-cohort
microceph   19.2.3+snapfd93b718e2   1701   squid/edge     canonical✓  in-cohort
microcloud  git-984ca0b             2219   latest/edge    canonical✓  in-cohort
microovn    24.03.6+snap77a702704c  1088   24.03/edge     canonical✓  in-cohort
snapd       2.75.2                  26865  latest/stable  canonical✓  snapd
```

2. Open a route for the MicroCloud VMs to be able to reach each other
```
# on Host A
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo ip route add 10.242.140.0/24 via 192.168.1.61 # IP of host B

# on Host B
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo ip route add 10.114.26.0/24 via 192.168.1.60 #IP of host A
```
3. Check connectivity between MicroCloud A and MicroCloud B
```
root@micro1:~# ping 10.242.140.10
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.242.140.10:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~#curl -k https://10.242.140.20:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.242.140.30:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.242.140.40:8443/1.0
```
4. Check connectivity between MicroCloud B and MicroCloud A
```
root@micro1:~# ping 10.114.26.10
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.114.26.10:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.114.26.20:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.114.26.30:8443/1.0
root@micro1:~# curl -k https://10.114.26.40:8443/1.0
```

5. Configure MicroCloud A `cluster links` and `replicator`
```
root@micro1:~# lxc auth group create clusters
root@micro1:~# lxc auth group permission add clusters server admin

root@micro1:~# lxc project create disaster-recovery
root@micro1:~# lxc project switch disaster-recovery
root@micro1:~# lxc auth group permission add clusters project disaster-recovery operator
root@micro1:~# lxc auth group permission add clusters project disaster-recovery can_edit

root@micro1:~# lxc edit deafult
name: default
description: Default LXD profile
config: {}
devices:
  eth0:
    name: eth0
    network: default
    type: nic
  root:
    path: /
    pool: remote
    type: disk
used_by: []
project: disaster-recovery


root@micro1:~# lxc cluster link create cluster_b --auth-group clusters
root@micro1:~# lxc replicator create replicator cluster=cluster_b snapshot=true --project disaster-recovery
root@micro1:~# lxc project set disaster-recovery replica.cluster=cluster_b
root@micro1:~# lxc project set disaster-recovery replica.mode=leader

```
6. Configure MicroCloud B `cluster links` 
```
root@micro1:~#lxc auth group create clusters
root@micro1:~#lxc auth group permission add clusters server admin
root@micro1:~#lxc project create disaster-recovery
root@micro1:~#lxc project switch disaster-recovery
root@micro1:~#lxc auth group permission add clusters project disaster-recovery operator
root@micro1:~#lxc auth group permission add clusters project disaster-recovery can_edit
root@micro1:~#lxc cluster link create cluster_a --token <token-from-A> --auth-group clusters
root@micro1:~#lxc project set disaster-recovery replica.cluster=cluster_a
root@micro1:~#lxc project set disaster-recovery replica.mode=standby
```

7. Start two instances on MicroCloud A (either containers or VMs) and ensure that they are running on different members. Instances on MicroCloud run on MicroCeph.
```
root@micro1:~# lxc list
+------+---------+---------------------+-------------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------+----------+
| NAME |  STATE  |        IPV4         |                      IPV6                       |      TYPE       | SNAPSHOTS | LOCATION |
+------+---------+---------------------+-------------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------+----------+
| c1   | RUNNING | 10.97.22.2 (eth0)   | fd42:2e75:4cca:11b7:216:3eff:fe33:90cc (eth0)   | CONTAINER       | 2         | micro1   |
+------+---------+---------------------+-------------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------+----------+
| v1   | RUNNING | 10.97.22.3 (enp5s0) | fd42:2e75:4cca:11b7:216:3eff:fefd:d184 (enp5s0) | VIRTUAL-MACHINE | 0         | micro2   |
+------+---------+---------------------+-------------------------------------------------+-----------------+-----------+----------+
```

8. Run replicator on MicroCloud A
```
lxc replicator run replicator
```
**Observed Behavior**
1. On MicroCloud B only `c1` was transferred
```
root@micro1:~# lxc list
+------+---------+------+------+-----------+-----------+----------+
| NAME |  STATE  | IPV4 | IPV6 |   TYPE    | SNAPSHOTS | LOCATION |
+------+---------+------+------+-----------+-----------+----------+
| c1   | STOPPED |      |      | CONTAINER | 1         | micro1   |
+------+---------+------+------+-----------+-----------+----------+
```
2. The snapshot was not taken on MicroCloud A
```
root@micro1:~# lxc storage volume list remote
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
|         TYPE         |                               NAME                               | DESCRIPTION | CONTENT-TYPE | USED BY | LOCATION |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
| container            | c1                                                               |             | filesystem   | 1       |          |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
| container (snapshot) | c1/snap0                                                         |             | filesystem   | 1       |          |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
| image                | 38a076c6ffe4decf5ad7671ee6737bb591dc7d33cdd5ef2592890ac3e412f1f4 |             | filesystem   | 1       |          |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
| image                | b83ccb4b14d3310bbd9c24b987a138d849fd09c903e4c15d91cad759ac25a6b3 |             | block        | 1       |          |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
| virtual-machine      | v1                                                               |             | block        | 1       |          |
+----------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+--------------+---------+----------+
```

3. If  `v1` is moved to `micro1` both instances are successfully transferred with their snapshots


### Information to attach

- [ ] Any relevant kernel output (`dmesg`)
- [ ] Instance configuration (`lxc config show <instance> --expanded`)
- [ ] Main daemon log (at `/var/log/lxd/lxd.log` or `/var/snap/lxd/common/lxd/logs/lxd.log`)
- [ ] If a lxc command fails, output of the command with `--debug`
- [ ] Output of the daemon with `--debug` (or use `lxc monitor` while reproducing the issue)
